label: input f, after n/w, in sequences starting with f or d (original phase)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.001% of steps). In the original phase it fires almost only when the input is the letter f (90% of mass) at positions 3-7, mostly t=4-5. It is strongly enriched when the sequence begins with f or d (first_tok f = 78% of mass), when the previous token is n or w (n = 71% of mass), and in sequences where d appears early (e.g. f d ... n f). The strongest activation is f d w 0 n [f]. Without the context conditions, plain f input has very low precision (0.1%). Even the full conjunction only reaches about 13% precision and 49% recall (64% of mass), so this is a narrow, conjunctive context detector that the per-step variables only partly capture. It essentially never fires in the copy phase, and does not fire at t<3 or on other tokens, apart from a handful of weak exceptions.
